summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a 5-day history of diffuse abdominal pain and low-grade fever following a recent hospitalization for catheter dislodgement and febrile neutropenia. Physical exam revealed rebound tenderness, and CT imaging showed colonic wall thickening at the hepatic flexure suggestive of non-specific colitis. He was initially treated with intravenous vancomycin and levofloxacin due to concern for infection in the setting of low white count. His symptoms improved, ANC remained above 1000, and he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. A new left lower lobe opacity on chest X-ray was noted but remained asymptomatic. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, resume lactulose, and follow up for kidney ultrasound and transplant evaluation. Blood and stool cultures remained pending at discharge.
